Press Releases | Congressman Thomas Suozzi Skip to main content Image Press Releases Suozzi (D-NY), Knott (R-NC), Cruz (R-TX), and Slotkin (D-MI) Introduce Bipartisan, Bicameral Right to Worship Act to Protect Worshippers August 6, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C.—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) and Congressman Brad Knott (R-NC), along with Senators Ted Cruz (R-TX) and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), introduced the Right to Worship Act in the House and the Senate, to establish a 100‑foot, protest‑free buffer zone around houses of worship during religious services, making it unlawful to knowingly disrupt or impede people from attending. This law imposes civil fines for violations and authorizes individuals, the U.S. Attorney General, and state attorneys general to sue violators. Peaceful expression protected by the First Amendment is excluded from the bill’s prohibited activities. SUOZZI REAPPOINTED TO POWERFUL HOUSE WAYS & MEANS COMMITTEE | Congressman Thomas Suozzi Skip to main content Image SUOZZI REAPPOINTED TO POWERFUL HOUSE WAYS & MEANS COMMITTEE January 7, 2025 Press Release Suozzi will fight for the restoration of the State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction and fair tax policy to address the cost of living for New Yorkers Washington, DC -  The Democratic Steering & Policy Committee announced today that Congressman Tom Suozzi (D—Long Island, Queens) has been reappointed to a coveted seat on the powerful House Ways and Means Committee, the chief tax-writing panel in Congress. He returns to the seat he held during the 116th and 117th Congresses. Mr. Suozzi will serve as the only Democrat from New York on the panel. "I am deeply honored to be reappointed to the House Committee on Ways and Means," said Suozzi, who is trained as a CPA and attorney. "This is not just an opportunity to serve my district but a chance to champion the priorities that matter most to hard-working families, particularly the urgent need to restore the SALT deduction," he continued. "I am especially grateful to my fellow New Yorker, Leader Hakeem Jeffries,"  said Suozzi . In 2021,  Crain's New York Business  said Suozzi "earned the nickname MR. SALT for his single-minded devotion to the issue." During his prior service, in part because of his persistence, the House passed three separate Suozzi bills to restore the SALT deduction with bipartisan support. Unfortunately, the bills died in the Senate. The Ways and Means Committee is the only Committee authorized explicitly in the U.S. Constitution of 1789 and, therefore, the oldest Committee in Congress. The powerful Ways and Means Committee is the chief tax-writing Committee in the House of Representatives. The Committee derives a large share of its jurisdiction from Article I, Section VII of the U.S. Constitution, which declares, "All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives."
